recordType.value: snapshot, with plaintext account_id set to the owning account

payloadShape.value: { date, value, note }, and no rate field of any kind

decimalScale.value: every quantity is parsed into a BigInt at a fixed scale of 12 decimal places, computed on as an integer, and formatted back to a string. No IEEE-754 float touches a value, a rate or a total, and no decimal library is pulled in

decimalRounding.value: multiplication rescales once, the integer product of two scale-12 values being scale 24 divided back by 10^12 with round-half-even. Addition and subtraction need no rescale. Division happens only in the percentage view and per-account interpolation and rounds half-even at scale 12 as well. Display rounding is a separate later step

valueInputBound.value: a value with more than twelve decimal places is rejected at input rather than silently truncated

canonicalValue.value: value keeps the fraction digits it was typed with, in the canonical form -?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\.[0-9]{1,12})?, and a zero carries no sign. Typed 12.50, 007, .5, 12. and -0.00 are stored "12.50", "7", "0.5", "12" and "0.00". Arithmetic reads the same string at scale 12. Reading never rewrites a value: a stored string stays as stored until the person changes it

confirmedValueIsTheStoredString.value: confirming writes the stored value string character for character, never the field's text parsed again, so a confirmed figure is never rounded or reformatted

untouchedAndEditedFields.value: a field is untouched while its text equals its prefill, which keeps a sweep row on Confirm and a recorded row's Save inert. An edited field is parsed and compared with the stored value as strings, not as numbers, so 12.50 typed over a stored "12.5" is an edit and writes "12.50"

dateFormat.value: YYYY-MM-DD, no time and no timezone

uniqueness.value: one snapshot per (account, date), a client-side rule the server cannot see

replacePromptRule.value: the replace prompt fires only where the stored figure is not already displayed in the field being edited, which is the single-holding form at a date the person chose. It does not fire in a reopened recording, and it does not fire in the archive dialog, which names the figure its zero replaces before its own confirm

upsertResult.value: on confirm, the existing record is updated in place: same record_id, version + 1, fresh nonce

confirming.value: confirming writes an ordinary snapshot with the same value string, a new date and a new record_id. No new field. It is one click for every kind of account with no branch between them, and it is unavailable for an account with no snapshots

recordingIsDerived.value: a recording is a date and nothing stores it. No fifth record type and no grouping record. It is a client-side index over the in-memory model, grouping snapshots and rate entries by their own date field. It exists exactly as long as a record carries its date, has no version, no author, no wall-clock time and no note of its own

recordingDateIsFixed.value: a recording's date does not move. Moving one entry between dates stays an edit of that snapshot from the holding's own page

openingWritesNothing.value: opening a recording writes nothing and fetches nothing. Not a version bump, not a nonce, not a rate request

createVersusReopen.value: which of the two happens is routing, decided before anything is typed. Asking for a new recording and picking a date the model already holds records for opens that recording's own screen, with no request and nothing created. Editing it is one Update away

preCreateReload.value: before the first record a sitting creates at a date, the client reloads the types it will create in, GET /api/records?type=snapshot and type=rate, and re-checks against freshly reloaded records rather than the model in memory. It runs once per sitting, not once per row. A sitting that creates nothing runs no reload

staleCreateRefusal.value: a save is refused whole when the reload finds the date recorded elsewhere, or finds any slot the save would create already taken, except the archive (archiveReloadScope). Nothing is written, not even into slots that are still free, and what was typed is lost with no draft buffer, no merge and no re-apply

clearingRule.value: a quantity cleared in a reopened recording deletes that snapshot. Only a field backed by a record at that date can be cleared: emptying a field prefilled from the holding's figure at another date deletes nothing. Clearing a quantity clears no rate. Clearing every quantity leaves the recording with its rates intact. Clearing carries no more confirmation than any other save. A DELETE answering Not Found counts as done. An archive's zero cannot be cleared while its holding is archived

deleteRecording.value: a separate action removes every record bearing that date, snapshots and rate entries together, under one confirmation stating that it is destructive and cannot be restored. Ordinary DELETE requests, quantities first and rates after, with no transaction spanning them. A partial delete leaves a recording, rolls nothing back and marks nothing half-deleted. The date is free afterwards, unless an archive's zero keeps it, and this is the only way a date becomes free

archiveZeroSurvivesRecordingDelete.value: the zero of a holding archived on that date is not deleted. The date remains a recording holding it, the confirmation says the zero stays, and a date holding archives' zeros and no prices offers no Delete

dateMoveOrder.value: a date move is a PUT of this record at the new date followed by a DELETE of the record being displaced, in that order. Delete-first risks losing the displaced record while the PUT fails

twoSnapshotsOnOneDate.value: a reachable state, surfaced and never silently resolved. The client picks neither, not by version and not by updated_at, renders both flagged in the account's history and in that date's recording with an action to keep one, and excludes that date from interpolation until resolved

priceNeverBlocksQuantity.value: nothing in the price half ever blocks a quantity, in any form: no disabled save, no required rate field, no warning to dismiss first. This file owns that rule and record-rate.md points at it

dateBounds.value: a future date is blocked. A date preceding the account's createdAt is allowed, because backfilling history is normal

valueRange.value: zero is valid and means a closed-out position, which is not the same as having no snapshot. Negative is valid, because net worth is a signed sum

archivedAccounts.value: an archived account takes no new snapshots, at any date. The archive's own zero is no exception, because it is written while the holding is still active, before archivedAt is set

archivedEntries.value: an archived holding's other entries stay editable and deletable, in value and note. An entry's date moves only to a date before the archive date, because onto it the move would displace the zero and after it the entry would be a figure after the archive. The date picker offers nothing from the archive date on. The archive's zero is read-only: no edit, clear or delete, on the holding's page or in the recording for its date. All client-enforced by construction, since the server sees neither a date nor archivedAt

archiveReloadScope.value: the archive is the one narrower case of the pre-create reload. It runs the same reload of both types, once, and is refused only when the archived holding's own slot at the date is taken. A date recorded elsewhere is the recording its zero joins, and a rate slot taken since is one its refresh leaves alone. This is the one exception to staleCreateRefusal

openedPricesLineLayout.value: on the single-holding form the opened prices line shows each unit's full name, its price and its source in full, without overlap or clipping, at any width. The rate lines always stack there, because the Dialog's content box is 416px, below the 720px the sweep's columns need. The sweep's own rate lines keep their columns only while their block is at least 720px wide and stack below it. A chip never exceeds its container and its text wraps rather than clipping

rollbackIsNotDetected.value: the AAD's version binds a ciphertext to the version it was written at but does not prevent a rollback of an intact (ciphertext, version) pair. Do not write a test asserting rollback is detected today

fixtures: a seeded vault of fifteen holdings across six symbols, for the sweep's one-reload and one-rate-request assertions
a decimal midpoint case that sits exactly on the half in both directions, for round-half-even on a scale-12 multiplication
typed inputs 12.50, 007, .5, 12. and -0.00, for the canonical-form assertion
under moneyPlaces 0, an XAU-ozt holding stored as "12.125" and a USD holding stored as "1000.40", for the confirm assertion

a holding stored as "12.5", for the sweep row offering Confirm, Record once edited, Confirm again when the prefill is typed back, and writing "12.50" when 12.50 is typed, and for the byte-identical record after display, opening its recording and confirming it at a new date

a second session whose in-memory model predates the first session's recording at a date, for the pre-create reload refusal, exercised both as a whole fresh recording and as one holding added inside a reopened one
a date holding a recording, a date holding only rate entries, and a free date, for the routing between create and reopen
a holding whose row on a reopened date is prefilled from its figure at an earlier date, for the clearing rule
a stubbed DELETE that fails, for the write-then-delete order on a date move and for the partial delete of a recording
a stubbed DELETE answering Not Found during a save, which must report as saved
two snapshots planted for one (account, date), for the flagged pair and the interpolation exclusion

an archived holding with its zero at the archive date and earlier snapshots, and a recording at that date holding other records, for the read-only zero, the date-move limit and the delete that keeps the zero
a unit with a long full name and a stored price whose provenance is the longest rendering, shown on the opened prices line of the single-holding form at a phone width and at a desktop width
focus: a figure the screen pre-filled into a row and nobody confirmed must appear nowhere afterwards. This is the single easiest rule in the product to satisfy on paper and to fake in a test: leave eleven of fifteen rows alone, save, and assert against the holdings' own record sets that no snapshot was created at that date for any of them, rather than against the sweep's own report of what it did

clearing every figure at a date must leave the recording standing with its rate entries byte-identical, and the recording must reopen showing its rate lines. A test that only checks the date still appears in a list proves nothing about the entries

clearing a field prefilled from another date must delete nothing and write nothing. The fake here is a test that clears a field backed by a real record, which passes whatever rule the implementation actually uses

the pre-create reload has to be asserted as a request count and a position: exactly one extra type reload, before the first row is written and none after it, and none at all for a sitting that only changes and clears. Both halves are invisible to an end-state assertion
the refusal of a save whose reload finds the date taken must be shown to have written nothing at all, including into slots that were still free. Checking the error message is the easy fake

the date move must issue the PUT before the DELETE, asserted with the DELETE stubbed to fail so that both records still exist afterwards. An implementation that deletes first passes every happy-path test

confirming must be asserted by reading the written record's value string against the source's, under moneyPlaces 0 and with values rounding would change ("12.125", "1000.40"). Checking the displayed figure, or a value that survives two places, passes an implementation that parses the prefilled text and writes it back

a stored string must be asserted unchanged after display, opening its recording and a confirm, by comparing the record byte for byte. A read path that normalizes "12.5" and writes nothing is invisible without that comparison, and one that does write is visible only there

the unchanged test is on strings: 12.50 typed over a stored "12.5" must write "12.50", and the prefill typed back must leave the row on Confirm. A numeric comparison passes both of the easy cases and fails these

round-half-even has to be asserted on a value sitting exactly on the midpoint in both directions. Any other case passes under round-half-up as well, and the rounding mode is what two implementations drift on
a Conflict inside a recording save must reload that row and retry nothing, with the stored record byte-identical afterwards. A retry that happens to succeed looks like correct behaviour

editing inside a reopened recording must never show the replace prompt while the single-holding form at an occupied date still does. Testing only one of the two directions leaves the rule half-asserted

the opened prices line on the single-holding form has to be asserted on rendered geometry at a narrow and a wide window: every unit's full name, price and source text present and visible, no chip wider than its container, no two boxes intersecting. A screenshot or a check that the text is in the DOM passes while the text is clipped or overlapped

an archive's zero must be asserted read-only against the controls: no edit or delete on the holding's page, no control on its row in the recording for its date, and no date from the archive date on in the picker for an earlier entry. The server cannot see any of it, so an API test asserts a rule that does not exist there

deleting a recording that holds an archive's zero must leave that record byte-identical and the date still opening, while every other record at the date goes. A delete that removes the whole date passes every ordinary delete test
do not write a test asserting that a rolled-back (ciphertext, version) pair is detected. The spec states outright that it is not, and a green test here would be asserting something untrue
